intro: If you're doing Chiang Rai on a backpacker budget but still want a base you can walk to the Night Bazaar and Jetyod Road from — Cat & Turtle is a small hostel that comes up among the cheap city-center stays · It isn't a designer flashpacker hostel; it sells on a friendly atmosphere, an easy walkable location and a price that starts at around THB 300/night for a dorm bed · There are private rooms too if you want a bit more privacy · This review is compiled from real guest reviews of stays in this area — we didn't stay ourselves.

body.html: Cat & Turtle is a small hostel in central Chiang Rai, and its main selling point is simple — a city-center location within walking distance of the Night Bazaar, the Clock Tower and Jetyod Road (Chiang Rai's bar and café strip) · For travellers without a vehicle who want to drop their bags and walk straight out to sightsee, that location is hard to find at this price · The place itself is plainly a true hostel rather than a styled boutique — you come to sleep, store your gear, and head out into the town.

Rooms come in two flavours — dorm beds for solo travellers on a tight budget, and private rooms for couples or anyone who wants a bit more privacy · Dorm beds start at around ฿300/night, while private rooms step up depending on size and whether they have a fan or air conditioning · Every room has free Wi-Fi · What guests in this area tend to mention is that the beds are more comfortable than expected for the price, and the sleeping areas are clean enough — but it's a budget hostel, so don't expect an en-suite bathroom in every room or a full set of amenities.
"Great location — easy walk to the Night Bazaar and the walking street, friendly owners, cheap. Perfect for backpackers who aren't fussy about luxury."

The real charm a hostel like this offers is its friendly atmosphere and a common area where you meet other travellers · The owners and staff tend to earn praise for being helpful — recommending places to eat and see, and helping arrange onward transport (to the White Temple and Black House, or buses to Chiang Mai or Chiang Khong) · For solo travellers, that's an edge a quiet hotel can't match — someone to talk to, people to swap tips with, and sometimes a group to go sightseeing with.

The honest things to know before booking — Cat & Turtle is a budget stay, and the trade-offs are typical hostel ones · Noise is the main one: the walls and soundproofing aren't solid, so you can sometimes hear the room next door or the street, especially near the Jetyod bar area at night · Some reviews in this area mention inconsistent housekeeping, towels and sheets you may need to ask to have changed, and a fairly smoker-friendly atmosphere that won't suit everyone · A pair of earplugs goes a long way here.

To be honest, Cat & Turtle isn't for travellers who want a perfectly quiet room, a smart en-suite bathroom or hotel-level service · But if you're a backpacker or budget traveller who weights a walk-to-the-Night-Bazaar location, a low price and a sociable atmosphere where you meet people — it does the job of a good hostel · Chiang Rai's best sights are spread out of town anyway (the White Temple, Black House, tea plantations), so having a cheap base in the center that you can walk out from in the evening is a sensible way to spend the budget.

The tip from reading reviews of stays in this area: if you're a light sleeper, ask for a room deeper inside, away from the street, and pack earplugs · If you're travelling as a couple, price up an air-conditioned private room first — in some periods the gap from a dorm is small but you get full privacy · And if you're heading to the White Temple or Black House, ask at the desk about transport or tours, because small hostels like this can often arrange it cheaper than booking online.

One last thing to know — it's a small property with few rooms, so it fills up fast in the cool high season (November–February) and during festivals · Prices and availability change often, so it's worth comparing several platforms and booking ahead if you're coming in peak season · Because online information for a small place like this is thin, read the latest reviews and double-check the exact map location before you book.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Cat & Turtle Chiang Rai

faq.q: Where is Cat & Turtle, and can you walk to the Night Bazaar?
faq.a: Cat & Turtle is a small hostel in central Chiang Rai, within walking distance of the Night Bazaar, the Clock Tower and Jetyod Road (the bar and café strip) · The location lets you explore at night without a vehicle · It's about 15 minutes by car from the White Temple and Mae Fah Luang Airport · As it's a small property, double-check the exact map location before booking.

faq.q: How much does Cat & Turtle cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around THB 300/night for a bed in a shared dorm · There are also private fan rooms and private air-conditioned rooms, priced by size and amenities · Prices and availability change often, especially in the cool season, so compare several platforms and book ahead for the best result.

faq.q: Who is Cat & Turtle best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for backpackers and budget solo travellers who want a city-center location walkable to the Night Bazaar, and who enjoy a sociable atmosphere where you meet fellow travellers · It's not the choice if you want a perfectly quiet room, an en-suite bathroom in every room, or hotel-level service.

faq.q: What downsides should I know before booking?
faq.a: The usual budget-hostel trade-offs — poor soundproofing (you hear the room next door and the street), basic amenities, and inconsistent housekeeping at times · Some reviews mention a fairly smoker-friendly atmosphere · It's worth asking for a room deeper inside, packing earplugs, and checking the room details before booking.

faq.q: Does Cat & Turtle have en-suite bathrooms and air conditioning?
faq.a: It varies by room type — dorm beds use shared bathrooms, while private rooms come with either a fan or air conditioning, and some have an en-suite bathroom · If you want AC and a private bathroom, specify it when you book and re-check the room details, as small properties often mix several room types.

faq.q: Where does this review's information come from?
faq.a: This review is compiled from real guest reviews of hostel stays in central Chiang Rai; our team did not stay in person · Because Cat & Turtle is a small property with limited online information, we recommend reading the latest reviews on booking platforms and verifying the current price and location before you decide.
